title: 1996 Air Africa crash
summary: Moscow Airways Antonov An-32B overran the runway while attempting to take off fully fueled and overloaded from N'Dolo Airport's short runway. The aircraft failed to achieve sufficient speed to bring its nose up, began to lift, and crashed into the Simbazikita produce market. The full fuel load ignited, creating a massive post-impact fire. Ground fatalities were estimated between 225 and 348, making this the deadliest aviation accident in African history and deadliest by ground casualties outside of terrorist attacks.
probable_cause: The aircraft was overloaded and fully fueled while attempting to take off from N'Dolo Airport's short runway. The aircraft did not achieve sufficient speed to bring its nose up yet began to lift prematurely, resulting in loss of control and crash into the market below.

factors.evidence: Aircraft attempted to take off fully fuelled and overloaded from N'Dolo Airport's short runway.
An-32B did not achieve sufficient speed to bring nose up yet began to lift.
Aircraft overran the runway at N'Dolo Airport.
Full fuel load ignited in crash into market, creating massive fire.

events.text: Aircraft begins takeoff roll from N'Dolo Airport's short runway while fully fueled and overloaded.
Aircraft does not achieve sufficient speed to bring nose up yet begins to lift, losing control.
Aircraft crashes into Simbazikita produce market full of shacks, pedestrians and cars.

title: ValuJet 592
summary: ValuJet Flight 592 crashed into the Florida Everglades about ten minutes after departing Miami on May 11, 1996. A fire developed in the cargo compartment caused by 144 expired chemical oxygen generators placed in cargo compartment boxes marked COMAT by maintenance contractor SabreTech. The fire caused progressive failure of the DC-9's electrical and flight control systems. All 110 people on board were killed, making it the deadliest aviation accident in Florida history.
probable_cause: Just before takeoff, 144 expired chemical oxygen generators were placed in the cargo compartment by ValuJet's maintenance contractor SabreTech, which violated Federal Aviation Administration regulations. The fire in the cargo compartment caused progressive failure of electrical and flight control systems leading to loss of control and crash.

factors.evidence: A fire developed in the cargo compartment caused by mislabeled and improperly stored chemical oxygen generators.
A flight attendant informed the crew of a fire in the passenger cabin.
144 expired chemical oxygen generators were placed in the cargo compartment in five boxes marked COMAT by maintenance contractor SabreTech.
The flight data recorder indicated progressive failure of the DC-9's electrical and flight control systems.

events.text: At 2:04 p.m. EDT, the DC-9 departed from Runway 9L and began a normal climb
At 2:10 p.m., passengers began to smell smoke and pilots heard a loud bang in their headsets
The sag in electrical power was determined to be the result of an explosion of a tire in the cargo hold
Kubeck and Hazen immediately asked air traffic control to return to Miami
Flight 592 disappeared from radar and crashed into the Everglades at a speed in excess of 507 mph

title: TWA 800
summary: TWA Flight 800, a Boeing 747 flying from New York to Rome via Paris, exploded in flight and crashed into the Atlantic Ocean off East Moriches, New York, twelve minutes after takeoff on 17 July 1996, killing all 230 aboard. The four-year NTSB investigation concluded that flammable vapors in the center fuel tank ignited, likely from a short circuit, after finding arcing in the fuel quantity indication system wiring that enters the tank; the captain had remarked on 'crazy' FQIS readings shortly before the explosion.
probable_cause: The NTSB determined the probable cause was an explosion of flammable fuel/air vapors in the center wing fuel tank, most likely ignited by a short circuit, with evidence of arcing found in the fuel quantity indication system wiring that enters the tank.

factors.evidence: Problems with the aircraft's wiring were found, including evidence of arcing in the fuel quantity indication system (FQIS) wiring that enters the tank.
The report's conclusion was that the probable cause of the accident was the explosion of flammable fuel vapors in the center fuel tank.
Several wide-ranging recommendations were made, which were incorporated into newer US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) standards.
The Boeing 747-100 performing this flight exploded and crashed into the Atlantic Ocean near East Moriches, New York, twelve minutes after takeoff.

events.text: About two minutes and thirty seconds before the explosion, the captain remarked about 'crazy' readings from the fuel quantity indication system.
At approximately 8:31 p.m. EDT, twelve minutes after takeoff, the Boeing 747 exploded and crashed into the Atlantic Ocean near East Moriches, New York.
NTSB investigators found evidence of arcing in the fuel quantity indication system wiring that enters the center fuel tank, a likely ignition source for the flammable vapors.
All 230 people on board were killed when the aircraft broke apart and crashed into the ocean, the deadliest air disaster investigation in U.S. history up to that time.
The four-year NTSB investigation approved its Aircraft Accident Report on August 23, 2000, and its recommendations were incorporated into new FAA fuel-tank safety standards.

title: Vnukovo Airlines 2801
summary: On approach to Svalbard Airport, the crew used outdated Jeppesen charts and set both HSIs to magnetic runway heading 283 degrees without using the localizer course. During the inbound turn, lateral deviation from the centerline grew due to inadequate wind drift correction. The aircraft reached Advent at 1,524 meters and turned late, resulting in a left (northeast) deviation from the correct track. Navigation at 1,524 m minimum altitude led to aircraft striking ground at Operafjellet during final approach, 3.7 km from the centerline.
probable_cause: A series of small navigational errors caused the aircraft to be 3.7 km from the approach centerline at the time of impact. The crew did not attempt to intercept the correct magnetic course and were probably not aware of VHF direction finding available at the airport.

factors.evidence: lateral deviation from the centerline at the time of impact was 3.7 km
crew did not attempt to intercept the magnetic course 155 degrees outbound from Advent
aircrew was probably not aware of VHF direction finding available at the airport and have not used it to confirm aircraft position
additional request for use of Runway 10 was again not understood because of the misunderstanding of the term runway in use
From 3000 m until impact, the flight was carried out in instrument meteorological conditions
aircraft reached 1524 m minimum altitude to Advent before striking ground at Operafjellet

events.text: Aircraft reached 1524 m minimum altitude to Advent, the initial approach altitude
Aircraft began base turn to magnetic heading 160 degrees but turn was started late resulting in aircraft flying northeast of correct outbound track
Crew started inbound turn but lateral deviation from correct track persisted
Aircraft descended to minimum altitude in instrument meteorological conditions from 3000 m
Aircraft struck ground at Operafjellet during final approach, 3.7 km from approach centerline

title: ADC Airlines 86
summary: ADC Airlines Flight 086 was descending to 16000 ft when Triax Flight 185 was assigned a conflicting altitude at 15000 ft. The Lagos ATC controller made a radar separation error, thinking Flight 086 was at 10000 ft when it was actually descending to 16000 ft. Flight 086's TCAS warned of traffic and the crew attempted evasive action. Following the TCAS alert, Captain Sama took control, but ATC directed a heading that led to loss of control and the aircraft crashed inverted in Lagos Lagoon at high speed.
probable_cause: Air traffic control separation error combined with loss of control during evasive maneuver.

factors.evidence: crew of the Boeing 727-231 operating the flight lost control of the aircraft while avoiding a mid-air collision on approach
controller immediately asked Flight 086 to redirect its heading to 300
pilot was also found to be at fault for proceeding on a heading of 330
TCAS of Flight 086 sounded an alert, warning the flight crews to reduce descent and start climbing in order to prevent a collision with Flight 185

events.text: Flight 086 took off from Port Harcourt and climbed to 24000 ft.
As the flight was approaching Lagos, ATC cleared Flight 086 to descend to 16000 ft.
The TCAS of Flight 086 sounded an alert, warning crews to reduce descent and start climbing.
Captain Sama immediately took over as the TCAS sounded the alert and the crew noticed the incoming Triax Flight 185.
ATC asked Flight 086 to maintain heading 300 while still descending toward an altitude conflict.
The aircraft lost control and crashed inverted at a very high speed into Lagos Lagoon.
